title: Borealis warehousing inference call notes — SKU sync + latency constraints
content:
Call: Borealis Warehousing — initial technical intake (30m)
Date: 2025-02-11 10:00 PT
Attendees: Alex Dunham (Borealis Eng), Priya Nair (Borealis Product), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Solutions), Tomás Rivera (Redwood Infra)

High-level ask (from Priya):
- Replace their rule-based SKU mapping + fuzzy search with an LLM-backed assistant that:
  - Normalizes incoming vendor SKUs and product descriptions
  - Suggests best-match canonical SKU (confidence + reasoning)
  - Runs in customer network (air-gapped possibility later) with strict PII controls
  - Needs fast throughput: 2k requests/min at peak, p95 latency target ~120ms (ideally <=100ms)

Notes / clarifying Qs from call:
- Data cadence: nightly feed of 3M new product rows + streaming updates (webhooks) for changed SKUs.
- Expected average doc length for generation: 120 tokens (description + metadata).
- Primary flow: call Redwood API for canonicalization and embedding-based recall to shortlist candidates, then LLM rerank.
- Customer cares about hallucinations: want provenance links to original vendor text and a confidence score.
- Security: key requirement to use their KMS + optional customer-managed HSM. Audit logs are mandatory for all inference calls.

Technical constraints we discussed:
- Private deployment is likely (VPC or on-prem VM group). Borealis currently prefers VPC + dedicated GPUs in Azure (eastus2) -> confirm instance types.
- Latency sensitivity suggests using a smaller, quantized reranker for initial pass and fallback to a full-quality model for low-confidence matches.
- Embeddings store: they already have Elastic + Postgres; prefer to keep vector index in their infra (FAISS/Weaviate) and call Redwood for rerank + normalization only.

Gotchas / risk areas noted during convo:
- SKU normalization requires access to vendor taxonomy mapping (semi-structured). Poorly normalized vendor text caused hallucinations in their previous ML attempts. Need prompt engineering + strict output schema (json with sku_id, confidence, reasons[]).
- Throughput/Batching: If we do continuous batching to hit cost targets, worst-case latency may spike. They want p95 guarantees. Need to scope Dedicated pool sizing and burst policy.
- Cost sensitivity: BOM for 2k rpm at p95 120ms could escalate if full-sized model used for every request. Recommend hybrid path.
- On-prem/air-gapped: they are exploratory. If true air-gap, need to plan model onboarding process and license checks offline.
- Data residency: EU customers present in Borealis supply chain -> region routing required.

Initial proposal ideas (sketch):
1) Two-stage pipeline (recommended):
   - Stage A: lightweight local reranker (quantized 7B) + embedding similarity filter (customer-run vector store) -> candidate list (top 10). p50 latency target ~35ms
   - Stage B: Redwood hosted/private full-quality reranker (or private deployment) for final canonicalization + structured JSON output + provenance. p95 target ~90-120ms depending on region
2) Output schema enforcement: use function-calling / structured output in the prompt. Include provenance fields and tokenized diff of source->normalized mapping.
3) Caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated vendor descriptions (retail SKU churn tends to have many duplicates). TTL policy suggestion: 24–72h for identical descriptions.
4) Fallback and graceful degradation: if Stage B capacity constrained, fall back to Stage A with lower-confidence flag and queue async verification.

Concrete engineering asks from us (actions we promised):
- Action 1: Infra sizing sketch for Dedicated pool to satisfy 2k rpm with p95 120ms. Marcus to produce estimate with GPU types and cost ranges. (Owner: Marcus; ETA: 2025-02-18)
- Action 2: Example output schema + prompt template for SKU canonicalization + provenance example. Samira to draft and circulate. (Owner: Samira; ETA: 2025-02-14)
- Action 3: Short demo flow: embed-based recall + Redwood rerank + provenance shown in UI (30min). Book for week of 2/24. (Owner: Alex + Samira; ETA: schedule by 2/20)
- Action 4: Compliance checklist for KMS/HSM + audit log retention + region routing. Tomás to map gaps versus Borealis requirements. (Owner: Tomás; ETA: 2025-02-21)
- Action 5: Quick PoC plan: 2-week pilot with synthetic feed (100k rows) hosted in Borealis dev VPC. Need NDAs and basic SSO. (Owner: Priya / Borealis)

Prompting / output notes (to self):
- Use strict JSON schema with an explicit "unknown" path to avoid hallucinations. Example keys: canonical_sku, confidence_score (0-1), reasons[], source_offsets[], provenance_ids[].
- Train prompt to include exact matching heuristics (string normalize rules) before model inference to reduce hallucination load.
- Consider running a lightweight regex normalization layer client-side (remove vendor codes, punctuation, normalize units) -> then call model for fuzzy mapping.

Edge cases they brought up:
- Bundled SKUs (multi-pack) where vendor description lists 3 SKUs in one line. Need to split and return multiple canonical suggestions.
- Images: some vendors send image URLs; Borealis wants eventual option to include image embedding similarity. Not in MVP.
- Rate-limiting: they expect bursty days (catalog refresh windows) — want autoscaling with quick warmup and predictable throttling policies.

Open questions to clarify on next call:
- Confirm Azure instance families they prefer (NVIDIA A10/A100?) and whether they have credits that affect SKU selection.
- SLA needs: do they want an uptime SLA for pilot or only for production? Any penalties?
- Vector store: confirm which vector db (FAISS/Weaviate/Pinecone) they will run in pilot.
- Retention window for audit logs (how long legally required per vendor region).

Meeting artifacts to attach in Confluence/Jira (create after we have Marcus estimate and Samira prompt):
- SE-842 (linked) will be the parent ticket for pilot run
- Confluence page: Borealis Onramp Notes (stub exists) -> update with architecture diagram + prompt templates

Quick risk mitigation ideas:
- For hallucination risk, enforce conservative confidence threshold and return "no confident match" instead of forcing a SKU. Customer product team is OK with fewer matches if precision is high.
- For latency risk, prewarm Dedicated pool during catalog refresh windows and use burst capacity with small warm-up buffers.

Notes to self (informal):
- Priya liked the idea of a visual diff in the UI showing vendor text -> canonical with highlighted tokens. Make a mockup in Figma with reasoning snippets.
- They mentioned a POC budget cap of ~$12k for first month of Dedicated usage — use Marcus estimate to see if that fits.
- Keep the pilot to a single region (eastus2) to simplify compliance and data residency for MVP.

Next steps summary (short):
- Marcus: infra sizing + cost (ETA 2/18).
- Samira: draft prompt + output schema + quick sample responses (ETA 2/14).
- Tomás: compliance/KMS/HSM checklist mapping (ETA 2/21).
- Alex/Priya: schedule demo week of 2/24 and confirm pilot participants + data sample (ETA schedule by 2/20).

TODOs (personal):
- Draft the prompt template and a bad/good example set (5 examples) before 2/14.
- Sketch UI mockup for visual diff (Figma) and link in Confluence.
- Prepare a short explainer for "hybrid rerank" cost tradeoffs for product to share with finance.

Random scribbles from call:
- "If it returns wrong SKU we pay restocking fee" — make sure product team understands precision tradeoff.
- Priya: "show me the evidence or we don't ship" -> provenance is must-have.

End of notes.

-- Samira
